MCC No. 609 of 2013
CLMA No. 10514 of 2013
IN
SA No. 13 of 2012
Hon’ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Mr. B.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate, Mr. 
Jayvardhan Kandpal, Advocate, present for the 
appellant. Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate, present 
for respondent No. 2. 
The appeal was dismissed for non 
prosecution on 27.05.2013. Restoration 
application has been filed along with delay 
condonation application as the restoration 
application was filed belatedly. Notices were 
issued to the respondents, in spite of notices 
they have not filed any objection as yet. 
Although Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate is 
represented respondent No. 2. 
In view of the above, fact, the delay 
condonation application is allowed as the 
ground urged for condoning the delay is bona 
fide. 
Also heard on the restoration application. 
The grounds are sufficient to allow the 
restoration application. 
Accordingly, the restoration application is 
allowed. The order dated 27.05.2013 is hereby 
recalled. 
Let the appeal be restored to its original 
number. 
List this appeal for admission in the week 
commencing 25.11.2013. 
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.) 
 25.10.2013
Aswal

orders.text:
SA No. 13 of 2012
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Kanwaljit Singh, Advocate for the 
appellant.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the 
respondents.
This Second Appeal, which was preferred in 
2012; for the last over eight years it is pending and 
it is yet to be argued on its admission.
Today, the matter was listed on a 
Substitution Application No. 10362/2020, whereby 
the learned counsel for the appellant has informed 
that the sole appellant has met with the sad demise 
on 18.09.2020.
Since the Substitution Application has been 
filed within the time, the same would stand 
allowed. The appellant’s counsel is directed to 
carry out the necessary amendment(s) in the cause 
title of the Second Appeal within a period of two 
days from today.
The learned counsel for the parties informs 
the Court that there is another connected Second 
Appeal No. 12 of 2012, which is also pending 
consideration.
The Registry is directed to list this Second 
Appeal along with Second Appeal No. 12 of 2012
on 07.12.2020. 
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 04.12.2020 Mahinder/

orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma
orders.text:
SA No.13 of 2012
With
SA No.12 of 2012
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Kanwaljeet Singh, Advocate for the 
appellants.
Mr. Harshpal Sekhon, Advocate appearing on 
behalf of respondents in S.A. No.13 of 2012. 
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Advocate for respondent 
nos.1 to 4 in S.A. No.12 of 2012.
The appellants herein have filed an application 
wrongly heading it to be under Order 41 Rule 1,
though it ought to have been under Order 41 Rule 27. It 
would be treated to be an application under Order 41 
Rule 27, which is yet to be taken into consideration 
because the appeals are yet to be argued on admission 
stage.
The respondents are represented through Mr. 
Harshpal Sekhon, Advocate, who submits that he has 
received instructions from the respondents today itself,
and he will be filling his authority on their behalf. The 
said applications are taken on record subject to the 
objections if any, to be filed by the respondents, which 
is to be considered at the stage of final hearing of the 
second appeal, yet again subject to the condition that 
the appeals are admitted. 
The counsel for the respondents may file his 
objection to the application under Order 41 Rule 27 
C.P.C., within a period of two weeks.
List this second appeal after two weeks. 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 17.12.2020

SA No. 13 of 2012

With
IA No. 13946 of 2021 
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Kanwaljit Singh, Advocate, for the 
appellant. 
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate, for the 
respondents. 
Mr. Akshay Pradhan, Advocate, for the 
applicant in IA No. 13946 of 2021. 
Out of the subsequent purchasers, one of 
whom happens to be Mrs. Deepti Singhal, is an 
applicant to the Application No. 13946 of 2021, 
which has been filed under the head of 
Impleadment Application, without referring to the 
provisions, under which, it has been filed. Though 
the pleadings in support thereto is based upon the 
conferment of right, on the proposed applicant to 
the Impleadment Application, by virtue of the 
subsequent sale deed executed in her favour. 
If a right is devolved on the basis of the 
subsequent purchase made during the pendency of 
the lease, the subsequent assignment made of the 
disputed property would be independently 
considered within the ambit of the provisions 
contained under Order 22 Rule 10 of the CPC.  Mr. Akashay Pradhan, the learned counsel 
for the applicant to the Impleadment Application, 
seeks to file an additional supporting affidavit to the 
Impleadment Application, clarifying as to under 
which provisions of law, the said Impleadment 
Application has been filed. 
He may do so on or before the next date 
fixed. 
List these Second Appeals on 18th July, 2022. 
In the meantime, Mr. Piyush Garg, the 
learned counsel for the respondents, may also file 
his objection, to the application under Order 41 
Rule 27 of the CPC, in compliance of the earlier 
order. 
 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 27.06.2022
Shiv
